playbooks.title: handoff.md template: continue a long Claude session in a new chat
playbooks.question: How do I continue a long Claude or ChatGPT session without losing context?
playbooks.answer: Ask the assistant to write a handoff file before you stop, then upload that file to a fresh chat. A good handoff lists the goal, what is done, what failed, the constraints and the next steps, so the new session does not repeat old mistakes.
playbooks.html:
Why a long AI session goes wrong

When one Claude or ChatGPT session runs for hours, the context gets messy. Wrong assumptions pile up and approaches that already failed get tried again. You get slower replies, weaker output and more rework.

The fix is simple: before you stop, ask the assistant to write a handoff file, then start a fresh session with that file.

How to use it

  1. Before ending a session, say: "Create a complete handoff.md file for this project."
  2. Save the file.
  3. Start a new chat and upload the file.
  4. Say: "Read this handoff file and continue from where we left off."

The handoff.md template

Copy this into a file and fill it in, or give it to the assistant as the format to follow.

# Project Handoff
## Project Name
[Project Name]
---
## Objective
What are we trying to achieve?
Example:
Build an AI automation agency website with premium animations and lead generation systems.
---
## Current Status
What has already been completed?
Example:
- Homepage completed
- Contact form completed
- Mobile responsiveness completed
- Hosting configured
---
## Current Problem
What specific issue are we solving right now?
Example:
Navigation animation breaks on mobile devices.
---
## Successful Attempts
Things that worked:
- Framer Motion animation setup
- Responsive layout fixes
- Form validation system
---
## Failed Attempts
Things that failed:
- CSS transform approach
- Animation library X
- Previous navigation implementation
Do NOT repeat these approaches.
---
## Key Decisions
Important decisions already made:
- React frontend
- Tailwind CSS
- Dark theme
- Minimal design style
---
## Constraints
Requirements that must be respected:
- Mobile first
- Fast loading
- SEO friendly
- No paid plugins
---
## Relevant Files
List important files:
- App.jsx
- Navbar.jsx
- Hero.jsx
- styles.css
---
## Next Recommended Steps
1. Investigate mobile animation issue
2. Test alternative animation approach
3. Validate performance impact
4. Deploy updated version
---
## Lessons Learned
Important findings:
- Library X causes conflicts
- Mobile Safari behaves differently
- Animation duration over 600ms feels slow
---
## Open Questions
Questions still unanswered:
- Best animation strategy?
- Alternative library?
- Performance tradeoffs?
---
## Final Instruction
Continue from the current state.
Avoid failed approaches.
Respect all constraints.
Focus only on solving the current problem.

The one-line command

Paste this at the end of any long session:

Create a detailed handoff.md file for this entire session.
Include:
- Objective
- Current State
- Successful Attempts
- Failed Attempts
- Constraints
- Lessons Learned
- Relevant Files
- Next Steps
Optimize it for a completely fresh Claude session so no context is lost and no failed approaches are repeated.

Where it helps

  • Software work: debugging, product builds, AI agents and automations.
  • Content work: research, scripts, newsletters and course material.
  • Business work: SOPs, strategy documents, operations and client projects.
  • Agency work: any client project that runs over several days and several people.
faqs: What is a handoff.md file?
It is a short text file that summarises a working session: the objective, current status, what worked, what failed, decisions, constraints and next steps. A new AI session reads it and carries on.
When should I start a new session?
When replies slow down, the assistant repeats an approach that already failed, or it forgets an earlier decision. Write the handoff, then start fresh.
Does this work in ChatGPT and Gemini too?
Yes. The file is plain text, so any assistant that accepts an uploaded or pasted file can use it.

playbooks.title: The LLM Council prompt: five expert views before one answer
playbooks.question: How do I get a more balanced answer from Claude or ChatGPT on a business decision?
playbooks.answer: Ask the assistant to act as a council: five advisors with different jobs (contrarian, first principles, expansionist, outsider, executor) analyse the problem, then a chairman settles their disagreements and gives one recommendation. The full prompt is below.
playbooks.html:
The idea

Most people ask an AI assistant one question and take one answer. A single answer misses risks and better options. This prompt makes the assistant argue with itself first: five advisors look at your problem from five angles, then a chairman weighs them and gives one recommendation.

The five advisors

  • The Contrarian looks for flaws: risks, weak assumptions and ways the plan fails.
  • The First Principles Thinker ignores industry habits and rebuilds the answer from basics.
  • The Expansionist looks for the bigger opportunity and points of leverage.
  • The Outsider knows nothing about your industry and questions what insiders take for granted.
  • The Executor cares only about what to do next: priorities, resources and an action plan.

The chairman

After the five have spoken, the chairman reviews every view, lists where they agree and disagree, settles the conflicts and gives a final recommendation with key insights, major risks, biggest opportunities and clear next actions.

The prompt

Act as an LLM Council.
I want five advisors to analyze my problem before providing a final answer.
Advisor 1: Contrarian
Find flaws, risks, weak assumptions and reasons this may fail.
Advisor 2: First Principles Thinker
Ignore conventional wisdom and rebuild the solution from first principles.
Advisor 3: Expansionist
Identify larger opportunities, leverage points and upside scenarios.
Advisor 4: Outsider
Analyze the problem as someone completely unfamiliar with the industry.
Advisor 5: Executor
Create a practical action plan focused on implementation.
After all advisors finish:
Act as Chairman.
Review every viewpoint.
Identify agreements and disagreements.
Resolve conflicts.
Provide a final recommendation.
Finish with:
- Top 3 Risks
- Top 3 Opportunities
- Next 7 Days Action Plan
- Final Verdict
My problem is:
[INSERT PROBLEM HERE]

Make them debate

Add this line at the end:

Challenge each other's reasoning before the Chairman provides the final verdict.

The advisors then argue with each other instead of giving five separate answers, which usually gives a deeper and more balanced result.

Questions it suits

  • A business decision: should we open a second branch this year?
  • Marketing: how should we win our first ten clients for a new service?
  • Hiring: should we hire a manager or promote from inside?
  • Product: should we build this feature or buy a tool?

It is a thinking aid. The decision, and the facts you feed it, stay with you.
faqs: What is the LLM Council method?
It is a prompt pattern in which one AI assistant plays several advisors with opposing viewpoints and then a chairman who reconciles them, so the final answer has been challenged before you read it.
Is the council's answer always right?
No. It shows more angles and risks than a single answer, but it works only from what you tell it. Check facts and numbers yourself.
Which AI tools does it work in?
Any capable chat assistant, including Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini.

playbooks.title: Business card to CRM: 10 AI prompts for event follow-up
playbooks.question: How do I turn business cards from an event into contacts and follow-ups using AI?
playbooks.answer: Photograph each card and ask an AI assistant to extract the details as structured data, then clean them into a sheet, score the leads and draft a personal follow-up for each. The ten prompts below cover every step.
playbooks.html:
What this set does

After a trade show or business event you come back with a stack of visiting cards. These ten prompts turn photos of those cards into a clean contact sheet, a follow-up message for each person and a priority list, using any AI assistant that reads images (ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini).

Use them in order: extract, clean, score, then write the follow-ups. Check the extracted phone numbers and emails against the card before you send anything.

1. Business Card Data Extraction

Analyze this business card image.
Extract and return the following fields in JSON format:
{
"full_name":"",
"job_title":"",
"company":"",
"email":"",
"phone":"",
"website":"",
"linkedin":"",
"address":""
}
Rules:
- Return only valid JSON.
- If information is missing use null.
- Fix OCR mistakes when obvious.
- Maintain proper capitalization.
- Verify email formatting.

2. Google Sheets Formatter

You are a CRM data cleaning assistant.
Convert extracted business card data into spreadsheet-ready rows.
Columns:
Name
Company
Position
Email
Phone
Website
LinkedIn
Lead Score
Assign Lead Score:
10 = Founder / CEO
8 = Director / VP
6 = Manager
4 = Executive
2 = Other
Output CSV format.

3. Personalized Follow-Up Email

Using this contact information:
Name: [NAME]
Company: [COMPANY]
Position: [POSITION]
Write a personalized networking follow-up email.
Requirements:
- Professional
- Under 120 words
- Mention meeting at an event
- Create curiosity
- End with a clear CTA
Output:
Subject Line
Email Body

4. CRM Notes Generator

Analyze this business card.
Generate:
- Industry
- Potential Pain Points
- Estimated Company Size
- Lead Priority
- Suggested Follow-Up Angle
Output concise CRM notes.

5. Lead Qualification Prompt

Evaluate this contact.
Score:
- Buying Power
- Authority
- Relevance
- Partnership Potential
Provide:
- Total Score
- Reasoning
- Recommended Next Action

6. LinkedIn Connection Request

Create a LinkedIn connection request.
Maximum 300 characters.
Context:
Met at [EVENT NAME]
Goal:
Build relationship without selling.

7. AI Sales Outreach

Create a personalized cold email using:
Name:
Company:
Role:
Requirements:
- Personalized opener
- Business-focused value proposition
- Soft CTA
- Human tone
Maximum 150 words.

8. Event Networking Summary

Analyze all extracted business cards.
Create:
- Top 10 highest-value leads
- Quick win opportunities
- Potential partnerships
- Follow-up priority list
Output as an action plan.

9. Google Sheets Automation Prompt

Create a workflow that:
1. Receives business card images
2. Extracts contact details
3. Cleans the data
4. Pushes data into Google Sheets
5. Sends a personalized follow-up email
6. Logs outreach status
Generate step-by-step workflow instructions.

10. Bulk Follow-Up Generator

Using this spreadsheet of contacts:
Generate unique follow-up emails for each contact.
Requirements:
- Avoid repetitive language
- Personalize by role
- Mention company
- Include CTA
Output in spreadsheet format.

A sensible routine after an event

  1. Photograph every card the same evening.
  2. Run prompt 1 on each photo, then prompt 2 to get one sheet.
  3. Run prompt 8 to pick the ten people worth a personal message.
  4. Send those ten a message you have read and corrected yourself. Use the bulk prompt only for the rest.
faqs: Can ChatGPT read a visiting card?

Yes. Assistants that accept images, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, can read a clear photo of a card and return the name, company, phone and email as structured text. Always check the result against the card.
How do I get the contacts into Google Sheets?
Ask for CSV output, as prompt 2 does, and paste it into a sheet. For a hands-free flow, an automation can receive the photo, extract the data and add the row.
Can this be fully automated?
Yes. Bizgenix AI builds this kind of flow: a card photo sent on WhatsApp becomes a CRM entry and a drafted follow-up.

playbooks.title: AI image upscale prompt that does not change the face
playbooks.question: What prompt upscales a photo with AI without changing the person's face?
playbooks.answer: Use a prompt that first lists what must stay identical (identity, facial proportions, expression, clothing, background and framing) and only then asks for sharper detail, better lighting and more depth. The full prompt is below.
playbooks.html:
What the prompt is for

You have a photo that is soft, low resolution or badly lit, and you want a sharper version without the AI changing the person. Most "enhance" prompts quietly alter the face. This one tells the model what it must not change, then what to improve.

It works in image tools that accept an uploaded photo and an instruction. Results vary by tool, so compare the output with the original before you use it.

The prompt

Upgrade the uploaded image into a pristine, ultra-high-definition cinematic version while preserving the subject with absolute fidelity. The person’s identity, facial anatomy, expression, body posture, clothing, accessories, environment, framing, and overall composition must remain completely unchanged. Do not modify, reinterpret, replace, or introduce any new visual elements. Reconstruct and refine micro-level details including precise facial contours, authentic skin texture with naturally visible pores, individually defined hair strands, sharp and lifelike eyes, and clean, well-resolved edges throughout the image. Enhance dynamic range, contrast, and dimensional depth using balanced, studio-quality cinematic lighting.

What it tells the model to keep

  • The person's identity, facial proportions and expression.
  • Body posture and position.
  • Clothing and accessories.
  • Background, framing and overall composition.
  • Nothing added, removed or replaced.

What it asks the model to improve

  • Facial contours and real skin texture, with visible pores and no artificial smoothing.
  • Individual hair strands and sharp, natural eyes.
  • Clean edges and fine detail across the frame, with compression marks removed.
  • Dynamic range, contrast, depth and balanced studio-style lighting.

Check before you publish

  1. Put the result next to the original and look at the eyes, teeth and hands first.
  2. If the face has changed at all, run it again or use the original.
  3. Never present an enhanced photo of a real person as an untouched photograph where that matters, such as identity documents or evidence.
faqs: Why does AI change faces when it enhances a photo?
Image models rebuild the picture rather than simply sharpening it, so they tend to redraw features. Telling the model exactly what to preserve reduces this, but does not remove it.
Which tools can use this prompt?
Any image tool that accepts an uploaded photo with a text instruction. Results differ between tools and versions.
Is the output safe to use for official documents?
No. An AI-enhanced photo is a reconstruction. Use an original photograph where authenticity matters.

playbooks.title: Business Brain: use Claude Code and Obsidian as your company memory
playbooks.question: How do I make Claude answer from my own business knowledge?
playbooks.answer: Keep your SOPs, client notes, meeting notes and research as files in an Obsidian vault and open that folder in Claude Code. The assistant can then search, summarise and advise from your own material; the ten steps and prompts are below.
playbooks.html:
What this is

A way to give Claude a memory of your business. You keep your knowledge as plain notes in Obsidian (a free note-taking app that stores files on your own computer) and open that folder in Claude Code. The assistant then answers from your clients, SOPs, meetings and research instead of from general internet knowledge.

Step 1: Create the vault

Download Obsidian from obsidian.md, install it and create a new vault called "Business Brain".

Step 2: Create the folders

Business Brain
├── Raw Sources
├── Wiki
├── Clients
├── SOPs
├── Meetings
├── Content
├── Research
├── Prompts
└── Projects

Step 3: Fill Raw Sources

Everything goes here first: books and PDFs you own, articles, transcripts of talks you learn from, podcast notes, industry reports and client documents.

Step 4: Build the Wiki

The Wiki is your company's own reference: lead generation, sales process, client onboarding, SOP library, marketing frameworks and offers. Anything important should end up here in your own words.

Step 5: Connect Claude Code

Open Claude Code and point it at the vault folder. It can now search your notes, organise them, write summaries and documentation, and draft workflows.

Step 6: Add your business knowledge

  • Clients: goals, problems, offers and deliverables.
  • Meetings: discovery calls, team meetings and client feedback.
  • SOPs: outreach, sales and delivery.
  • Research: competitors, industry reports and trends.

Keep confidential client data out unless your agreement with the client and your own data rules allow it.

Step 7: Link the notes

Inside Obsidian, link related notes, for example Lead Generation → Cold Outreach → Message Scripts → Client Acquisition. The links show the assistant how topics relate.

Step 8: Ask for a knowledge map

Analyze my entire vault and create a structured knowledge map.
Identify:
- Missing information
- Duplicate information
- Weak systems
- Improvement opportunities
Provide recommendations.

Step 9: Use it as an advisor

Act as my business advisor.
Use only information found inside my vault.
Reference supporting notes whenever possible.
Challenge weak assumptions and suggest improvements.

Step 10: A weekly review prompt

Act as my Chief Operating Officer.
Analyze my entire Obsidian vault.
Identify:
- Bottlenecks
- Growth opportunities
- Missing systems
- Revenue leaks
- Content opportunities
Use evidence from my notes and provide an action plan with priorities.
Reference the source notes used for every recommendation.

A weekly rhythm

  • Monday: add new notes.
  • Tuesday: tidy the Wiki.
  • Wednesday: review research.
  • Thursday: draft content from the vault.
  • Friday: update SOPs.
  • Saturday: run the knowledge-map prompt.

The more of your own knowledge the vault holds, the more specific the answers become.
faqs: What is Obsidian?
A free note-taking app that stores notes as plain text files on your own computer. Because they are ordinary files, an AI coding assistant can read them.
Is my data sent to the AI company?

The notes stay on your computer, but any text the assistant reads to answer you is sent to the AI provider. Check the provider's privacy settings and keep confidential client data out unless you are allowed to share it.
Do I need to know coding?
No coding is needed to follow these steps, but Claude Code runs in a terminal or desktop app, so allow an hour to set it up the first time.

playbooks.title: How to make a product video ad with ChatGPT and Google Flow
playbooks.question: How do I make an AI video ad for my product from one photo?
playbooks.answer: Upload a clean product photo to ChatGPT and ask it to write a cinematic video prompt, then paste that prompt into Google Flow with the photo as the reference image. Generate several versions in 9:16 and keep the one where the product is shown accurately.
playbooks.html:
What you need

  • One clean photo of your product.
  • ChatGPT, to write the video prompt.
  • Google Flow, Google's AI video tool, to generate the clip.
  • Optional: your brand name, offer and audience.

Step 1: Take a clean product photo

Use one front-facing image: plain background if possible, product clearly visible, good light, no blur, no collage.

Step 2: Ask ChatGPT for the video prompt

Upload the photo to ChatGPT and paste this:

I want to turn this product image into a premium 8-second AI video ad.
Analyze the product image and create a Google Flow video prompt for a cinematic product commercial.
The output should include:
1) Product analysis
Identify:
- what the product is
- likely target audience
- visual style that would suit it
- premium emotions / brand vibe it should communicate
2) Ad concept
Create 3 different ad angles for this product:
- Luxury / premium
- Problem-solution / performance
- Aesthetic / viral social ad
3) Final Google Flow prompt
Write one polished Google Flow video prompt for the strongest ad concept.
The prompt should include:
- camera movement
- lighting
- environment / background
- product motion
- cinematic details
- texture / reflections / atmosphere
- premium ad style
- vertical 9:16 framing for social media
4) Shot direction
Give me a short shot breakdown:
- opening shot
- hero close-up
- motion / reveal shot
- ending brand shot
Keep the final video prompt clean and ready to paste into Google Flow.

Step 3: Pick one angle

  • Luxury: perfumes, skincare, watches, jewellery, fashion.
  • Problem and solution: gadgets, kitchen tools, supplements, utility products.
  • Social: trend-led products and reels.

Step 4: Generate in Google Flow

  1. Open Google Flow and start a new project.
  2. Choose Video.
  3. Upload your product photo as the reference image.
  4. Paste the prompt ChatGPT wrote.
  5. Set the aspect ratio to 9:16 for reels and Shorts, and a length of 6 to 8 seconds.

Menu names in Flow change from time to time; look for the option that adds an image as a reference or start frame.

Step 5: Make several versions

Generate three to five versions with small changes: stronger lighting, a different camera move, a cleaner hero shot, more atmosphere. The quality comes from this iteration, not from one prompt.

Step 6: Judge the result

  1. Product clarity: can you see the product clearly, and is it your product, with the right label and shape?
  2. Feel: does it look like an advertisement or like random AI footage?
  3. Motion: is the camera move smooth?
  4. Brand fit: would you post it under your brand name?

If any answer is no, generate again. Add your text and call to action in your normal video editor.

The prompt formula

[product] + [setting] + [lighting] + [camera movement] + [texture details] + [brand feel] + [aspect ratio]

Three example prompts

A luxury perfume bottle on a glossy black reflective surface, golden rim lighting, floating mist, slow cinematic push-in, premium reflections, ultra-detailed glass texture, high-end commercial look, 9:16 vertical ad
A premium skincare serum bottle on wet stone with soft water droplets, clean beauty ad aesthetic, gentle camera orbit, bright luxury lighting, minimal background, realistic product texture, 9:16 vertical
A premium sneaker floating above a dark textured floor, dynamic side lighting, slow rotation, dust particles, sporty cinematic ad look, crisp product details, bold contrast, 9:16 social ad framing

Before you run it as a paid ad

AI video can change a label, a logo or the shape of a product. Check every frame against the real product, and do not show a result or feature the product does not have.
faqs: What is Google Flow?
Google's AI video tool. It creates short clips from a text prompt and can use an uploaded image as a reference.
How long should an AI product ad be?
Six to eight seconds is enough to test an idea on reels or Shorts. Add text and a call to action in your video editor.
Can I run the result as a paid advertisement?
Only after checking that the product, label and claims are shown accurately. AI video can alter a logo or shape, and an ad must not show something the product does not do.

playbooks.title: 100 ChatGPT prompt shortcuts (and how to make them work)
playbooks.question: Do ChatGPT "secret codes" like /Expose really exist?
playbooks.answer: No. ChatGPT has no hidden commands of that kind. They are short names for instructions, and they work once you paste the instruction or save the list in Custom Instructions; the 100 shortcuts and their instructions are below.
playbooks.html:
Read this first

These are not hidden commands built into ChatGPT. Each one is a short name for an instruction. ChatGPT only behaves this way when it knows what the name means.

There are two ways to make them work:

  1. Paste the instruction. Copy the sentence next to the shortcut into your message.
  2. Save the list once. Paste the shortcuts you use into ChatGPT's Custom Instructions (Settings → Personalization), or into a Project, with the line "When I type one of these shortcuts, follow the instruction next to it." After that, typing the shortcut alone is enough.

They work the same way in Claude and Gemini.

Thinking and strategy

  • /Expose Reveal the real problem behind my question, the assumptions I’m making, and what I’m actually trying to solve. Then answer from that deeper level.
  • /KillCritique Don’t be polite. Critique my idea brutally. Tell me what’s weak, unrealistic, likely to fail, and how to fix it.
  • /10xThink Think 10x deeper before answering. Give me the most strategic, nuanced, high-leverage response possible.
  • /IQ200 Answer like a world-class expert with elite reasoning, but keep it practical and actionable.
  • /AutoSpy Analyze my prompt for hidden biases, weak assumptions, blind spots, and flawed logic before answering.
  • /DevilsAdvocate Argue against my idea like a smart skeptic. Show me the downside, the flaws, and the counterarguments.
  • /ReverseEngineer Reverse engineer how a top 1% operator would solve this from scratch.
  • /FirstPrinciples Strip away assumptions and explain this from first principles.
  • /BlindSpots Tell me what I’m not seeing, what I’m ignoring, and what could hurt me later.
  • /StressTest Stress test this plan under worst-case scenarios, competition, low budget, and bad execution.
  • /DecisionMode Compare the options, show the tradeoffs, and tell me which path has the highest upside.
  • /SecondOrder Go beyond the obvious and explain the second-order consequences of this decision.
  • /RootCause Don’t treat the symptom. Find the real root cause of the problem.
  • /NoMercy Be direct. Don’t protect my feelings. Give me the answer I need, not the one I want.
  • /OperatorMode Answer like a founder/operator who only cares about leverage, speed, and ROI.
  • /PatternRecognition Identify the pattern behind this problem and show me where it usually leads.
  • /LeverageFirst Show me the highest-leverage moves first instead of the easiest moves.
  • /ConstraintBreak Find the bottleneck stopping growth and show me how to remove it.
  • /TruthFilter Remove hype, cope, and wishful thinking. Tell me what’s actually true.
  • /SimplifyHard Make this simple without making it dumb.

Writing and copy

  • /RewriteBetter Rewrite this to sound sharper, cleaner, more persuasive, and more human.
  • /HookMode Turn this idea into 10 high-retention hooks using curiosity, shock, authority, and outcome angles.
  • /SalesMode Rewrite this to sell better without sounding pushy. Focus on pain, desire, proof, and action.
  • /Shorten Cut the fluff and make this 50% shorter while keeping the punch.
  • /Humanize Make this sound less robotic and more like a smart human wrote it.
  • /CTAUpgrade Give me 10 stronger CTAs that increase comments, clicks, or replies.
  • /HeadlineLab Write 20 headline variations with different angles: curiosity, fear, benefit, speed, status.
  • /ClarityPass Make this easier to understand, tighter, and cleaner.
  • /MakeItPunchy Increase rhythm, sharpness, and memorability line by line.
  • /StoryMode Turn this into a story with a stronger setup, conflict, payoff, and lesson.
  • /AuthorityTone Rewrite this so it sounds credible, calm, and high-status.
  • /CasualTone Make this sound conversational, natural, and not over-polished.
  • /LuxuryTone Rewrite this to feel premium, exclusive, and high-value.
  • /ControversyMode Make this more polarizing and scroll-stopping without sounding stupid.
  • /EmotionalPunch Increase emotional weight, tension, and relatability.
  • /Skimmable Rewrite this so it’s easy to scan on mobile.
  • /HookAudit Score these hooks out of 10, explain why they’re weak, and rewrite the best 5.
  • /BodyFix Fix the middle of this script so retention doesn’t drop after the hook.
  • /CloserFix Rewrite the ending so it feels stronger, cleaner, and more persuasive.
  • /OneLiner Turn this into a punchy one-liner or quote.

Content creation

  • /Virality Turn this into a viral short-form content idea with hook, body, payoff, and CTA.
  • /ContentMachine Turn this one idea into 10 reels, 5 carousels, 3 lead magnets, and 3 email ideas.
  • /CarouselMode Turn this topic into a high-retention Instagram carousel slide by slide.
  • /ReelScript Write a 30–45 second reel script with a text hook, verbal hook, body, and CTA.
  • /ThumbnailIdeas Give me 10 thumbnail concepts with emotion, curiosity, and contrast.
  • /TitleBank Write 20 titles for this content idea across YouTube, Reels, and carousels.
  • /HookVariations Write 25 hook variations for this same idea in different styles.
  • /BrollPlan Tell me exactly what to show on screen for every line of this script.
  • /CommentCTA Give me comment CTAs that drive replies and DMs without sounding desperate.
  • /DMLeadMagnet Turn this piece of content into a “comment X and I’ll DM you” funnel.
  • /ContentGap Tell me what this script is missing to make it actually worth watching.
  • /RetentionFix Rewrite this script for higher retention with faster pacing and stronger open loops.
  • /CreatorClone Study this creator’s style and write content in a similar structure without copying them.
  • /TrendAngle Turn this topic into a trend-based content piece that feels current.
  • /SeriesMode Break this topic into a 7-part content series.
  • /AuthorityBuilder Turn this topic into content that makes me look smarter, more credible, and more trusted.
  • /MythBuster Turn this into a myth-busting post with strong “you’ve been lied to” energy.
  • /ContrarianTake Give me a non-obvious, contrarian angle on this topic that still makes sense.
  • /DemoMode Turn this into a step-by-step demo video idea with visuals.
  • /Repurpose Turn this YouTube script into a reel, carousel, tweet thread, and email.

Business and sales

  • /Monetize Show me how to turn this idea, audience, skill, or asset into revenue.
  • /OfferAudit Audit my offer. Tell me why it’s weak, unclear, low-value, or hard to sell.
  • /PositioningFix Fix my positioning so the right buyers instantly understand why I matter.
  • /LeadGenPlan Give me a lead generation plan for this niche with channels, messaging, and daily actions.
  • /PricingHelp Tell me how to price this offer based on value, demand, and positioning.
  • /ClientCloser Help me close clients for this service with offer framing, objections, and call flow.
  • /ObjectionCrusher List the top objections buyers will have and give me responses that actually work.
  • /NicheResearch Break down this niche: pain points, buying triggers, offers, and content opportunities.
  • /CompetitorTearDown Analyze my competitors, show me where they’re weak, and how I can position against them.
  • /AcquisitionPlan Give me a realistic client acquisition strategy for the next 30 days.
  • /RevenueMap Show me the fastest path from where I am now to my target monthly revenue.
  • /OfferStack Build me a ladder of offers: free, low-ticket, core offer, upsell, and premium.
  • /CashFlowFix Show me how to increase cash flow fast with what I already have.
  • /RetentionPlan How do I keep clients longer, increase LTV, and reduce churn?
  • /UpsellEngine Find upsell opportunities inside my current service or product.
  • /DMCloser Write DM conversations that move leads from interest to booked call.
  • /SalesPageFix Audit this sales page and tell me exactly what’s killing conversions.
  • /MarketMessageFit Make sure the messaging matches what the market actually wants to hear.
  • /ProofBuilder Show me how to create stronger proof, case studies, and credibility if I’m still small.
  • /LeadsToday Give me the fastest ways to get leads today, not “build a brand for 12 months.”

Productivity and execution

  • /StepByStep Break this into a step-by-step action plan with zero fluff.
  • /SOPMode Turn this process into a clean SOP someone else can follow.
  • /AutomationIdeas Show me what parts of this workflow can be automated with AI or no-code tools.
  • /PriorityStack Tell me what to do first, second, and third based on ROI and urgency.
  • /TimeSaver Cut this workflow down to the minimum time required without losing output quality.
  • /ExecutionPlan Turn this goal into a 7-day, 30-day, and 90-day execution plan.
  • /DailySystem Build me a daily operating system to make progress on this consistently.
  • /DelegationMode Tell me what to delegate, what to keep, and what to automate.
  • /TemplateBuilder Turn this repeated task into a reusable template.
  • /ChecklistMode Turn this into a checklist I can run every time.
  • /DeepWork Structure this project so I can finish it with focused work blocks.
  • /EnergyAware Build this workflow around low energy, distraction, and inconsistency.
  • /MomentumFix Tell me why I keep stalling and how to create momentum again.
  • /BottleneckAudit Find the one bottleneck slowing everything down.
  • /WeeklyReview Create a weekly review system so I don’t drift or waste time.
  • /SpeedRun Give me the fastest possible version of this plan if I only have 7 days.
  • /MinimalViable What’s the smallest version of this I can launch or test immediately?
  • /AntiOverwhelm Turn this messy plan into something simple and executable.
  • /FocusFilter Tell me what to ignore so I stop doing fake work.
  • /DoneByTonight Give me the exact plan to make meaningful progress on this before tonight.

Examples

/KillCritique I want to start a second showroom in Surat. Here is my plan…
Here is my sales page. /SalesPageFix /ObjectionCrusher /PositioningFix
/SOPMode Turn this voice note on how we dispatch orders into an SOP.

Shortcuts that work well together

  • Decisions: /Expose + /AutoSpy + /DecisionMode + /SecondOrder
  • Writing: /RewriteBetter + /ClarityPass + /MakeItPunchy
  • Getting work done: /StepByStep + /PriorityStack + /DoneByTonight
  • Business review: /OfferAudit + /PositioningFix + /LeadGenPlan

The value is in the instruction behind each name. A shortcut does not make the answer true: check facts, numbers and names before you use them.
faqs: Are these official ChatGPT commands?
No. They are prompt shortcuts written by the Bizgenix AI team. ChatGPT follows them only when the instruction is in the message, in Custom Instructions or in a Project.
Where do I save them in ChatGPT?
Settings → Personalization → Custom Instructions, or the instructions of a Project. Add one line telling ChatGPT to follow the instruction next to each shortcut.
Do they work in Claude and Gemini?
Yes. Save them in a Claude Project or a Gemini Gem in the same way.

playbooks.title: 73 Claude prompt shortcuts (and the exact instruction behind each)
playbooks.question: Do Claude "secret codes" like /redteam or /deepthink really exist?
playbooks.answer: No. Claude has no hidden commands or secret modes. Each shortcut is a short label for a specific instruction that works once you paste it or save the list in a Claude Project; all 73 shortcuts and their full instructions are below.
playbooks.html:
Read this first

Claude has no built-in "secret codes" or hidden modes. Every shortcut below is a short label for a concrete instruction. Typing /redteam or INVERT alone does nothing unless Claude already has the instruction in your Claude Project instructions or in the same message.

How to make all 73 shortcuts work:

  1. Paste one instruction directly into your prompt whenever you need that behaviour.
  2. Save the list in a Claude Project (Project Instructions) with the opening rule: "When I start or end a message with any shortcut below, apply its exact instruction to my request."
  3. Verify facts yourself. Shortcuts change how Claude analyses or writes—they do not verify numbers, legal rules or product claims.

Copy-ready Project setup line

When I include one or more shortcuts below (such as /redteam or INVERT) in a message, follow the exact instruction written next to each shortcut. Never invent statistics, client names or dates; mark missing facts clearly.

Core Writing & Style

  • /ghost — Rewrite this draft in plain, direct prose: use short sentences, active voice and concrete words, cut filler and corporate clichés, and preserve all facts untouched for final human editing.
  • /mirror — Study the writing samples I paste here—sentence length, vocabulary, punctuation and structure—and rewrite my draft to match that exact style without inventing new facts.
  • /punch — Make every sentence shorter and more direct: put the main verb early, cut adjectives and qualifiers that add no meaning, and remove throat-clearing openings.
  • /hook — Give me five distinct opening lines for this piece that earn attention with a specific fact, question or tension—no clickbait and no generic summaries.
  • /trim — Cut this text by at least 30% without losing a single fact, number or action item; flag any sentence you kept only for transition.
  • /polish — Tighten grammar, flow and clarity so the draft reads professionally to a client or executive while keeping the exact meaning and tone intact.
  • /flow — Reorder paragraphs and add clean transitions so each idea leads naturally to the next from opening answer to closing action.
  • /rephrase — Rewrite this passage in three structurally different ways—one executive summary, one conversational note, and one bulleted brief—keeping every fact identical.
  • /voice — Lock in the tone, reading level and phrasing rules I specify above and keep them consistent across every reply in this conversation.

Artifacts & Creation

  • ARTIFACTS — Build a self-contained, working interactive file (HTML/React/SVG/document) I can test immediately, and list any assumptions or sample data clearly.
  • /buildme — Design and build a small working tool from this description: keep dependencies minimal, label sample data clearly, and list how to run and verify it.
  • DASHBOARD — Create an interactive summary view for the metrics I provide: highlight exceptions first, show period comparisons, and keep calculations transparent.
  • PROTOTYPE — Build the smallest testable version of this workflow in one pass so I can try the user flow on sample records before scoping a full build.
  • BLUEPRINT — Map out the architecture, file layout, data flow, edge cases and acceptance tests for this project before writing any implementation code.
  • WIREFRAME — Lay out the screen hierarchy, sections, copy slots and primary user action in clean text/HTML structure without spending effort on decorative styling.
  • GENERATOR — Build a reusable template or script that accepts my structured inputs and outputs consistent, ready-to-review deliverables on demand.

Thinking & Reasoning

  • OODA — Analyse this situation in four explicit stages—Observe (raw facts only), Orient (constraints and context), Decide (trade-offs and choice), and Act (first concrete step).
  • /deepthink — Break the problem into assumptions, constraints, second-order effects and failure modes step by step before recommending a direction.
  • L99 — Skip surface-level generalities: give me an operator-level analysis with concrete constraints, edge cases, exact trade-offs and measurable checks.
  • CHAINLOGIC — Show each step of your reasoning from starting facts to conclusion so I can inspect and challenge any link that looks weak.
  • /blindspots — List five important questions, risks or missing data points I have not mentioned yet that could invalidate this plan.
  • OVERTHINK — Stress-test every detail of this decision: examine edge cases, timing clashes, hidden costs and human-handoff failures before we commit.
  • /unpack — Deconstruct this complex topic into its moving parts, explain how each part works in plain words, and show how they depend on one another.
  • INVERT — Instead of asking how to succeed, list every reliable way this project could fail or stall, then design rules to prevent each one.
  • XRAY — Strip away buzzwords and framing to state what is actually happening underneath: incentives, bottlenecks, real numbers and who decides.

Learning & Mastery

  • /teachme — Teach me this concept step by step as a practitioner: explain why it matters, give a concrete business example, and ask me one check question before moving on.
  • GAPFINDER — Assess what I already know from my summary below, pinpoint the exact concepts or skills I am missing, and order them from highest impact to lowest.
  • /eli5 — Explain this simply using everyday words and a familiar Indian business analogy—zero jargon, short sentences, clear takeaway.
  • MASTERCLASS — Teach this subject at practitioner depth: mental models, real trade-offs, common mistakes made by teams, and how experts verify quality.
  • SPEEDRUN — Give me the 20% of concepts and steps I need to understand and apply in the next 30 minutes to get a working result safely.
  • /mentor — Advise me like an experienced operator who knows my constraints: tell me directly what to prioritise, what to drop, and what to ask next.
  • CRASHCOURSE — Give me a structured five-minute briefing: core definition, why it matters, three worked examples, and three cautions.

Analysis & Strategy

  • /redteam — Attack this plan aggressively from the perspective of a sceptical buyer, competitor and auditor; list every weak claim, cost risk and execution flaw.
  • PARETO — Identify the few inputs, customers, products or tasks in this list that account for most of the result, and say what can safely wait.
  • WARGAME — Simulate how competitors, customers and regulators are likely to react over the next two quarters if we make this move.
  • /premortem — Imagine it is six months from now and this initiative failed completely: write the most probable reasons it failed and the early warning signs we ignored.
  • LEVERAGE — Find the single bottleneck or change in this workflow where one unit of effort improves multiple downstream outcomes.
  • /audit — Review this work against clear acceptance criteria: list factual gaps, unclear ownership, formatting errors and unverified claims.
  • BOTTLENECK — Trace this process from input to cash or completion and identify the exact step where work piles up, waits or fails most often.
  • /scenario — Model three scenarios from these inputs—conservative, base and downside—showing the assumptions, cash/time impact and trigger to switch plans.

Creative & Content

  • /viral — Rewrite this core idea with three sharper angles built around a concrete mistake, number or counter-intuitive truth from real work—no clickbait.
  • HOOKS10 — Write ten distinct opening hooks for this topic—using questions, contrast, specific numbers and real situations—and label who each hook fits.
  • /storysell — Turn this dry feature or lesson into a short real-world narrative: situation, friction, decision, what changed, and one takeaway for the reader.
  • REMIX — Combine two unrelated frameworks or examples from my notes into one fresh, practical post outline with a clear point of view.
  • /angles — Give me ten genuinely different content angles on this single topic—for owners, finance heads, operations teams and sceptics.
  • CLIFFHANGER — Write three closing lines that invite thoughtful discussion or point naturally to the next step without sounding forced or salesy.
  • /captionme — Write three concise social captions for this post or video: put the searchable topic phrase in line one, keep the body crisp, and end with one clear action.
  • POLARIZE — State a clear, defensible point of view on this industry habit—explain what most people do wrong, why it hurts, and what to do instead.
  • /banger — Condense this insight into one memorable, plain-spoken sentence worth quoting—no clichés and no exaggerated claims.

Coding & Technical

  • /debug — Trace this bug systematically: list the most likely root causes from the error and code shown, how to verify each in one command, and the minimal fix.
  • REFACTOR — Simplify this working code without changing behaviour: remove duplication, split mixed responsibilities, and keep interfaces backward-compatible.
  • /shipit — Review this code as a pre-release check: identify missing validation, error handling, edge cases, secrets exposure and tests to run before deploying.
  • ARCHITECT — Propose a clean system design for these requirements: components, data schema, boundaries, failure recovery and what not to build yet.
  • AUTOMATE — Turn this manual multi-step task into a repeatable script or workflow with clear inputs, dry-run checks, logs and a stop/rollback rule.
  • /optimize — Find the real performance or payload bottleneck first using measurements, then suggest targeted changes with expected impact and trade-offs.

Research & Deep Dives

  • /deepdive — Investigate this topic thoroughly across mechanisms, pricing, constraints, failure modes and alternatives; separate verified facts from open questions.
  • FACTCHECK — Inspect every claim, statistic and quote in this draft: mark what is verified from provided sources, what is unverified, and what needs a dated citation.
  • /investigate — Examine this problem like an analyst: list what evidence we already have, what is contradictory, and the exact primary checks needed to settle it.
  • TRENDSCAN — Summarise what has actually changed in this market or toolset recently based on verifiable releases and buyer behaviour—skip hype.
  • /digest — Distil this long document into a one-page executive brief: core thesis, key numbers with dates, decisions required and open risks.
  • DOSSIER — Compile a structured briefing on this company, product or topic using only verified facts: overview, positioning, strengths, gaps and sources.

Power Commands

  • /godmode — Use full structured reasoning for this task: state assumptions, explore alternatives, check numbers and edge cases, and deliver an execution-ready output.
  • /autoprompt — Turn my rough goal below into a clear, structured prompt with Role, Context, Task, Constraints, Input placeholders and Output Format.
  • MEGAPROMPT — Build a comprehensive reusable prompt template for this recurring workflow, including quality gates, edge-case handling and review steps.
  • PERSONA — Adopt the specific practitioner role I name—such as a chartered accountant, operations head or B2B buyer—and evaluate this strictly from their seat.
  • /memory — Summarise the confirmed rules, facts, decisions and preferences established in this conversation into a clean context block I can paste into future chats.
  • PROMPTFIX — Diagnose why my prompt below gave weak output and rewrite it with clear criteria, constraints and concrete examples.

Direct & Decision Modes

  • /nofilter — Skip politeness and padding: tell me plainly what is weak in this idea, what assumptions look unrealistic, and what you would change first.
  • BEASTMODE — Hold the output to the highest practical standard: verify logic, tighten every section, flag weak evidence and leave zero placeholders unless marked.
  • CEOMODE — Evaluate this strictly as a business owner accountable for cash, time and reputation: focus on ROI, risk, team bandwidth and this week’s decision.
  • /negotiate — Prepare a structured negotiation brief: our walk-away line, the other side’s likely priorities, concessions to trade, and exact responses to three objections.
  • FOUNDER — Think like an owner-operator building with a lean team: favour fast proof on real customers, low fixed overhead and repeatable systems.
  • SENTINEL — Act as final quality control before this ships: scan for factual errors, unapproved claims, missing links, broken edge cases and unclear instructions.

Shortcuts that work well together

  • Before launching a service or offer: /unpack + /redteam + /premortem
  • Before publishing an article or client draft: /audit + FACTCHECK + /trim + SENTINEL
  • Weekly business review: BOTTLENECK + PARETO + CEOMODE

Checked against Claude's Project and prompt behaviour on 28 Nov 2026. No unprovable claims (such as "undetectable AI writing") are included; always review drafts in your own voice and check every number.
faqs: Are these built-in Claude commands?
No. Claude does not ship with hidden slash commands like /redteam or /ghost. They only work when you provide the instruction in a Claude Project or paste it into your message.
Where should I save them in Claude?
Open a Claude Project, paste the setup line and your chosen shortcuts into Project Instructions once, and every new chat inside that Project will recognise them.
Can a prompt make AI text undetectable?
No tool or prompt guarantees "undetectable" writing. Use clear instructions to cut filler, then edit the facts and examples in your own voice.
